site_name: Switch Core Campus (LAS VEGAS 2, 4, 5, 7-12 and later buildings)
serving_utility: NV Energy (Nevada Power Company) wires for delivery only; energy bought from a third-party supplier (Morgan Stanley as of 2019) under NRS 704B
load_basis: Built power capacity, not metered load: Switch FY2021 10-K lists the Core Campus's nine open facilities (LAS VEGAS 2, 4, 5, 7-12, opened 2003-2019) at 'up to 311 MW' as of 2021-12-31. Capacity added 2022-2025 (LAS VEGAS 14, 15, 16 appear in OpenStreetMap) is NOT included because only directory sites give figures for those buildings. Actual draw is not public and is likely well below nameplate.
notes: Campus-level record. Coordinates are LAS VEGAS 7 (the original SUPERNAP 7) from OpenStreetMap. Same campus as known fids osm:way/172739950, 585998677, 585998678, 617194689, 984796364, 1017048670, 1263819877, 1314355599, 1421212901, 1558897570, and Switch's definition of the Core Campus also covers the older East Sahara buildings LAS VEGAS 4 and 5 (osm:way/1017460713, osm:way/1017460715); do not double count them. The 10-K says the 2003 opening is the earliest Core facility; LAS VEGAS 7 itself opened in 2008. The 10-K states Switch has bought power 'directly from the national market' since 2017-06-01 after unbundling from the incumbent utility; the Nevada Independent names the 704B process and Morgan Stanley as supplier. The 10-K listed five further Core facilities (180 MW) as 2022+; switch.com/las-vegas now says 'up to 495 MW of power upon completion' (https://www.switch.com/las-vegas/). A 2017 Switch release put the campus at 'up to 315 MW' after LAS VEGAS 10 (https://www.switch.com/switch-core-campus-opens-las-vegas-10-data-center/).

serving_utility: NV Energy (Sierra Pacific Power Company) wires for delivery; energy bought from a third-party supplier under NRS 704B
load_basis: Built power capacity, not metered load: TAHOE RENO 1 'up to 130 MW' (Switch FY2021 10-K) plus TAHOE RENO 2 'up to 55 MW' (Switch one-sheet, which says it was 'opening May 2024'; the opening itself is not independently confirmed). TAHOE RENO 3, 4 and 5 appear in OpenStreetMap but no citable source gives their status or size. Actual draw is not public.
notes: Campus-level record. Coordinates are the TAHOE RENO 2 building from OpenStreetMap; TAHOE RENO 1 is the inventory point bi:762-0 about 1 km east. Same campus as known fids osm:way/1116775095, 1320683840, 1494498031, 1494498032; do not double count. The 10-K gives the first data center's opening as November 2016 (press coverage dates the public opening to February 2017), so our_start_year 2018 looks late. Utility confidence is medium because the 704B arrangement is documented (the Switch one-sheet advertises a '704b power purchasing option' at this campus, and Switch's 2016 exit approval covered its Tahoe Reno facility), but that Sierra Pacific is the delivering utility is inferred from service territory. Full buildout: 'up to 2 Gigawatts' per the 2024 one-sheet; the FY2021 10-K planned 650 MW (130 open + 520 future). Wikipedia, citing Data Center Frontier (2020), reports 127 MW of planned behind-the-meter solar at Citadel; not verified here.

Same campus as osm:way/844359207. NV Energy asked the Nevada PUC (reported January 2020) to approve an energy supply agreement and tariff under which it would procure 350 MW of solar and up to 280 MW of storage to serve this data center; this pass did not find the commission's final order, hence medium confidence on the arrangement. First-operation year not established: Google's site page says only that it broke ground in 2019 and that the Henderson and Storey County data centers 'were built in 2019 and 2021, respectively' (https://datacenters.google/locations/henderson-nevada/); trade press in January 2020 expected a mid-2020 start, and a 2020-09-22 Area Development report expected opening in 2021 (https://www.areadevelopment.com/newsItems/9-22-2020/google-data-center-storey-county-nevada.shtml). The inventory's 2020 is therefore plausible but unconfirmed; 2021 is equally supported. No citable load figure found; the inventory's 241 MW was left alone.

No independently sourced coordinates; keep the inventory point. Google and NV Energy filed (June 2024) a supply agreement under a new Clean Transition Tariff: NV Energy buys output of Fervo's 115 MW Corsac Station geothermal project and credits it against Google's bills at its Storey County data centers. Google reported on 2025-05-13 that the Nevada PUC approved it (https://blog.google/feed/nevada-clean-energy/). The 115 MW is a supply contract for a project still under development, not a measure of site load. Year: Google's page says the site 'was built in 2021' and a September 2020 report expected it to be operational in 2021; neither is a dated in-service announcement, hence medium. Which NV Energy operating company serves the site is inferred from territory (northern Nevada). No citable load figure found; the inventory's 161 MW was left alone.

site_name: Apple Reno data center (Reno Technology Park)
load_basis: Average load implied by Apple's reported electricity use for the Reno data center in fiscal 2024: 454 million kWh / 8,784 hours = 51.7 MW. This is actual consumption, not nameplate; fiscal 2024 is the latest year published in the report used.
notes: Match to the unnamed OpenStreetMap buildings is an inference from location: the ways are tagged building=data_center with source 'WC GIS' (Washoe County GIS), sit beside I-80 in Washoe County ZIP 89434, and Apple's is the data center at Reno Technology Park. Same campus as known fids osm:way/775412066, 775412067, 775412068, 775412069, 775412072, 775412073, 1210199365, 1210199366, 1210199367, 1210199368; do not double count. Apple's report says the site has been in service since December 2012 and is supplied through NV Energy, including the NV GreenEnergy Rider agreements that Apple, NV Energy and the Nevada PUC set up (Fort Churchill ~20 MW, Boulder Solar II 50 MW, Techren II 200 MW, Turquoise 50 MW). Classed as special_contract because each rider agreement is a PUC-approved customer-specific arrangement on top of utility service. That the operating company is Sierra Pacific is inferred from territory.

load_basis: Not established. The building is designed for 60 MW (six 10 MW halls) but at the July 2025 launch the 'remaining capacity' was not due until 2026, and no source says how many halls were energized in 2025.
notes: New site, not in known_facilities (distinct from PowerHouse bi:1259-0). 300,000 sq ft on 20 acres with a dedicated on-site 100 MW NV Energy substation (https://www.novva.com/data-center-facilities/tahoe-reno-nevada/). Novva announced the launch on 2025-07-08; its 2023 announcement targeted late 2024 and one trade report says a first phase opened in late 2024, so 2024 is possible. Street address not confirmed: secondary sources disagree (1 Astro Way, McCarran versus 3399 Peru Drive), so coordinates are left null. Service is listed as ordinary retail because no special contract surfaced; the operating company is inferred from territory.

load_basis: Not established. Operator describes a 275,000 sq ft, 100 MW design with a 100 MW owner substation; energized capacity in 2025 is not published.
notes: New site, not in known_facilities. Novva's July 2025 Tahoe Reno launch release lists North Las Vegas among its existing facilities, so it was operating by mid-2025, but no opening date, street address or utility was found in a citable source. North Las Vegas lies in Nevada Power (NV Energy) territory; that is a territory inference only and is not recorded as a finding. A second North Las Vegas campus is in development.

load_basis: Not in commercial operation during 2025 according to the operator's own timeline: construction Q3 2024 to Q2 2026, utility power delivery Q4 2025, first delivery April 2026.
notes: Update to an existing record: the inventory's start year of 2025 appears to reflect permit or power-delivery timing rather than operation. Operator page lists 49 acres, up to 3 two-story buildings, 900,000 developable sq ft and 200 MW. The 2026 year is a published plan, not a confirmed in-service date, hence low confidence. No address or utility on the operator page; keep the inventory coordinates.
